## Deliverable

The gateway polls the OpenCode Go account usage endpoint with its own key and admits the opencode rail only on a fresh account reading under the policy ceiling — a Go twin of GW-CODEX-HEADROOM, specified as rows in GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT §Capacity — closing the `⚑ gap (2026-11-01, PR #3105 → work #3108)` flag.

Child of Goal #3118 (acceptance 1). Operator-filed; rewritten to the queue-ready shape by island intake — the original evidence is kept below.

## Acceptance

1. GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT §Capacity gains a Go headroom block (reports / verdicts / admission / poll) with the key rows below; every row is a `rule("GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT")` test in `gateway/tests/test_sessions_admit_capacity.py` against a fake usage endpoint, green.
2. A policy **without** `rails.opencode.headroom` admits the Go rail exactly as today (row "no headroom block keeps today's admission") — the deployed `policy.json` and the byte-identical `policy-default` world are NOT touched by this PR (the loader refuses unknown keys; the deployed block is Goal #3118's post-launch leg).
3. The index flag `⚑ gap (2026-11-01, PR #3105 → work #3108)` is deleted from the GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT row on the page's coupling table and in `gateway/specs/README.md`; the "⚑ gap: the Go account headroom" and "⚑ gap: the Go draw is the gateway's own traffic only" rows are deleted; the "Go window draw" bullet states it is a lower bound of the one account pool, kept as a belt under the reading ⚖.
4. The PR body carries `Spec changes:` (rule 1).

## Spec changes

Requirement: `GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT` on `gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md` — world `policy-go` (new, beside `policy-codex`: `rails.opencode.headroom` = `max_age_s` 120, `ceiling` 0.95, windows `rolling` / `weekly` / `monthly`, `poll_interval_s` 30 — fixture values ⚖, never code literals). A worker session `{platform, worker}` whose walk reaches the opencode rail; now = T.

| description | usage endpoint answer (polled at T−10) || decision | reason | retry_after_s |
|---|---||---|---|---|
| "a fresh Go reading under the ceiling admits the opencode rail" | rolling 20 %, weekly 46 %, monthly 36 %, all `status: ok` || dispatch on opencode | — | — |
| "the rolling block at the ceiling defers until its reset ⚖" | rolling 95 % resets T+1000, weekly 46 %, monthly 36 % || defer (opencode was the last candidate) | quota-limited | 1000 |
| "two exhausted windows wait for the later reset ⚖" | rolling 96 % resets T+1000, weekly 97 % resets T+8000 || defer | quota-limited | 8000 |
| "a window whose status is not ok limits ⚖" | rolling 20 % `status: limited` (any value ≠ `ok`) || defer | quota-limited | 60 (`defer_retry_s`) — verify the vendor's non-ok spelling during implementation |
| "no reading yet is unknown — fail closed" | no poll answered || defer | quota-unknown | 60 |
| "a stale reading is stale" | polled T−10, asked at T+115 || defer | quota-stale | 60 |
| "a missing window refuses the whole report" | `monthly` absent || report refused (`quota-invalid`); verdict unchanged | — | — |
| "a passed resetsAt is refused" | rolling `resetsAt` ≤ T || report refused (`quota-invalid`) | — | — |
| "a limited Go rail is skipped, the walk continues" | rolling 96 %; a later rail has capacity || dispatch on that rail | — | — |
| "no headroom block keeps today's admission ⚖" | world `policy-default` (no `rails.opencode.headroom`), endpoint unreachable || dispatch on opencode (window draw + account latch as today); no poll sent | — | — |
| "the poll carries the Go key and no identity reaches a log" | one poll || `GET <usage URL>` with `authorization: Bearer <go key>`; the URL from config with no default (unset = no poll ⚖) | — | — |

Translation pin: each of `usage.rolling` / `usage.weekly` / `usage.monthly` → `{used_percent: percent, resets_at: resetsAt (RFC 3339 → epoch), window: <name>}`; the profile is keyed by window NAME, not minutes (the monthly window is anchored at the subscription anniversary, not a fixed length) ⚖. `percent` is 0–100 (observed `0`, `46`, `36`) — verify the type (int vs float) during implementation.

Index row: delete `⚑ gap (2026-11-01, PR #3105 → work #3108): the Go account headroom is unread — the rail's one shared allowance is learnt from a ride's first 429 (the "⚑ gap: the Go account headroom" row)` from the GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT row on the page's coupling table, and `· ⚑ gap (2026-11-01, PR #3105 → work #3108): Go account headroom unread` from `gateway/specs/README.md`.

Unverified: the vendor's `status` values other than `ok`, `percent`'s numeric type, whether `/zen/go/v1/usage` and `/inference/go/v1/usage` differ — verify during implementation against one live poll with the gateway's key (record the observed payload shape with synthetic values as `gateway/tests/fixtures/go-usage-observed.json`, as codex did).

## Out of scope

- The deployed `policy.json` headroom block, the usage-URL env on the deployment, and `policy-default` — Goal #3118's post-launch leg (after this image is deployed).
- The no-strike-after-429 outcome rule — the sibling child of #3118 (GW-SESSIONS-OUTCOME).
- Go gauges (`gateway_subscription_utilization{rail="opencode"}`, a `gateway_go_usage_poll_total` family) beyond a log line per poll outcome.
- The agent-runtime half (finalize classifying `usage limit exceeded`).

## Evidence (from the original filing, 2026-11-01)

- The vendor reading, probed 200 with the gateway's own key: `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` (also `/inference/go/v1/usage`) → `{"usage":{"rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-11-01T14:26:16Z"},"weekly":{"status":"ok","percent":46,"resetsAt":"2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"},"monthly":{"status":"ok","percent":36,"resetsAt":"2026-11-13T11:15:25Z"}}}`. Account-level only (no per-model split, no absolute amounts); `rolling` = a 5-hour block anchored at first use (20 % of the monthly allowance), `weekly` Monday 00:00Z (50 %), `monthly` the subscription anniversary (100 %).
- One account allowance across every paid model: OpenCode support, anomalyco/opencode#54875 (the docs still say per model, anomalyco/opencode#60311).
- Gateway log 2026-11-01 (Loki, ns `agent-egress`): `capacity: opencode 429 on opencode-go/minimax-m3.1-flash — cell cooled for 6945 s` at 01:39:01Z; claude-haiku-5-5 at 01:44:10Z and mimo-v2.6-pro at 01:47:25Z, each admitted fresh after the first and 429'd on its first call against the same reset.
- Ride transcripts: `s3://agent-transcripts/homelab/issue-3087/worker-r1-20261101T013911Z/`, `…/issue-2589/worker-r1-20261101T014419Z/`, `…/issue-2589/worker-r1-20261101T014735Z/`.
- Sizing: plan Go = $60 weighted/month, $12 per 5-hour block; weight = 60 ÷ the model's listed monthly limit (minimax-m3.1-flash 3×, the $15 models 4×). The gateway's rides sent 1369 Go requests (~$3.4 at list on minimax) in the five hours before the strike — one worker pod empties the block.

The work item behind the GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT index flag `⚑ gap (2026-11-01, PR #3105 → work #3108)` — the "⚑ gap: the Go account headroom" row PR #3105 adds to `gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md` §Named gaps. Rule 10's flag must name a live work issue; this is it. Not an agent-loop item until the seat queues it (no `agent/*` label).

## Gap

The OpenCode Go plan is **one account allowance** across every paid model (OpenCode support, anomalyco/opencode#54875; the docs still say per model, anomalyco/opencode#60311). PR #3105 made a Go 429 latch the whole rail (`latch_scope: account`), but the gateway still learns of an exhausted 5-hour block only from the **first 429 of a ride** — and the `opencode` harness does not survive one (three retries, then `Error: Go usage limit exceeded`, exit). On 2026-11-01 01:39–01:47Z three worker rides died mid-work that way (#3087, #2589 ×2), finalize classified them `unknown`, and the FU-200 fleet rule latched three issues (#3095).

The vendor publishes the account reading. Probed 200 with the gateway's own key:

```
GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage        (also /inference/go/v1/usage)
{"usage":{"rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-11-01T14:26:16Z"},
          "weekly":{"status":"ok","percent":46,"resetsAt":"2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"},
          "monthly":{"status":"ok","percent":36,"resetsAt":"2026-11-13T11:15:25Z"}}}
```

Account-level only (no per-model split, no absolute amounts); `rolling` is a 5-hour block anchored at first use (20 % of the monthly allowance), `weekly` Monday 00:00Z (50 %), `monthly` the subscription anniversary (100 %). The gateway's existing per-model `window_draw` is a lower bound of that one pool (and sees only its own rides), so it cannot replace the reading.

## Done when

1. A Go twin of [GW-CODEX-HEADROOM](https://gateway-specs.homelab.teststuff.net/endpoints/openai-responses/#gw-codex-headroom): the gateway polls the usage endpoint on `rails.opencode.headroom.poll_interval_s`, keeps one strictly-newer report, admits the opencode rail only while every window's `percent` is under the policy `ceiling`, and otherwise defers `quota-limited` with `retry_after_s` = the binding window's `resetsAt`; `quota-stale` / `quota-unknown` as the codex rule has them (fail closed). Rows in GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT §Capacity against a fake usage endpoint (the `policy-default` world); the deployed `policy.json` carries the `headroom` block **in a second PR after the image that reads it is deployed** (the loader refuses unknown keys — README §Test).
2. The per-model `window_draw` on the opencode rail is retired or demoted to the ⚑ gap it now is (the shared pool makes it a lower bound); the "⚑ gap: the Go account headroom" and "⚑ gap: the Go draw is the gateway's own traffic only" rows close together.
3. A consumer outcome on a session whose **last relayed upstream answer was a 429** counts no model strike (GW-SESSIONS-OUTCOME): the gateway owns the transport fact first-hand, and a capacity death is not a verdict on the model — the rule that would have kept #3095's three issues off `agent/error` even with a missed latch. (The agent-runtime half — finalize learning `usage limit exceeded` as a capacity class, the launcher's case list mapping it — is a separate agent-runtime item; this one is the gateway's.)

## Evidence to carry

- Gateway log 2026-11-01 (Loki, ns `agent-egress`): `capacity: opencode 429 on opencode-go/minimax-m3.1-flash — cell cooled for 6945 s` at 01:39:01Z; claude-haiku-5-5 at 01:44:10Z and mimo-v2.6-pro at 01:47:25Z, each admitted fresh after the first and 429'd on its first call against the same reset.
- Ride transcripts: `s3://agent-transcripts/homelab/issue-3087/worker-r1-20261101T013911Z/`, `…/issue-2589/worker-r1-20261101T014419Z/`, `…/issue-2589/worker-r1-20261101T014735Z/`.
- Sizing: plan Go = $60 weighted/month, $12 per 5-hour block; weight = 60 ÷ the model's listed monthly limit (minimax-m3.1-flash 3×, the $15 models 4×). The gateway's rides sent 1369 Go requests (~$3.4 at list on minimax) in the five hours before the strike — one worker pod empties the block.
